about: Strategy cards for /arena and diversified subagent execution. Every agent gets exactly one card: one reasoning mode, one workflow, one strategy. 15 × 12 × 12 = 2,160 distinct cards. The dealer spreads them with no repeats and covers every axis before repeating. Add entries freely — IDs must be unique within each list.

reasoning.name: First principles
reasoning.how: Strip the task down to the facts and requirements nobody can argue with. Rebuild the answer from those alone, and keep a convention only if it earns its place again.

reasoning.name: Inversion
reasoning.how: Ask what would make this answer fail. List every way it could, then build the answer that makes each of those failures impossible.

reasoning.name: Analogy
reasoning.how: Find a problem in a different field that has already been solved and has the same shape. Port its solution over, then fix every place where the analogy breaks.

reasoning.name: Adversarial
reasoning.how: Picture the harshest expert reviewer trying to tear the answer apart. Write their attacks down first and build the answer backwards from them.

reasoning.name: Constraint first
reasoning.how: List every hard constraint, stated and implied: time, budget, tools, format, audience, platform. Solve strictly inside that box and let the tightest constraint drive the design.

reasoning.name: Worked example
reasoning.how: Solve one concrete, realistic instance end to end first, with real values. Generalise only from what that example actually taught you.

reasoning.name: Socratic
reasoning.how: Interrogate the task with the questions a sharp expert would ask before starting. Answer each one explicitly and let the answers decide the shape of the solution.

reasoning.name: Contrarian
reasoning.how: Write down the obvious default answer, then argue seriously against it. Keep only what survives the argument, even if that takes you the unpopular way.

reasoning.name: Systems thinking
reasoning.how: Map the moving parts, how they affect each other, and what happens second and third order. Optimise the whole system, not just the one part the task points at.

reasoning.name: Decomposition
reasoning.how: Break the task into independent sub-problems. Solve each one completely, then integrate them and test the seams where they meet.

reasoning.name: Working backwards
reasoning.how: Describe the finished result precisely, as if it already exists. Then work backwards, step by step, to where the user is right now.

reasoning.name: Probabilistic
reasoning.how: Assign rough probabilities to assumptions and outcomes. Commit to the highest-expected-value path. Flag assumptions whose probability matters most.

reasoning.name: Red team
reasoning.how: Become an adversary trying to break, exploit, or misuse the solution. Fix every vulnerability the adversary finds before submitting.

reasoning.name: Bayesian update
reasoning.how: Start with a prior answer, then update it systematically as each new piece of information or constraint comes in. Show which updates mattered most.

reasoning.name: Opportunistic
reasoning.how: Scan for the highest-leverage intervention — the one change that solves the most problems or unlocks the most value. Build the solution around that leverage point.

workflows.name: TDD
workflows.how: Write the test or acceptance criterion first. Then write the minimum implementation to pass it. Refactor only after it passes.

workflows.name: Scratch and refine
workflows.how: Produce a rough first draft at speed. Then make a dedicated second pass to fix gaps, tighten the prose, and raise quality.

workflows.name: Outside-in
workflows.how: Start from the user-facing interface or output. Work inward toward implementation, letting the interface drive every design decision.

workflows.name: Bottom-up
workflows.how: Build and verify the smallest primitives first. Compose them into larger structures only once each primitive is solid.

workflows.name: Spike and stabilise
workflows.how: Explore the riskiest unknown with a throwaway spike. Once the unknown is resolved, implement the real solution cleanly.

workflows.name: Checklist driven
workflows.how: Build an explicit checklist of every requirement before writing a word of the answer. Tick off each item as it is addressed.

workflows.name: Structured debate
workflows.how: Produce two or three candidate solutions. Argue for and against each. Commit to the winner and justify the choice.

workflows.name: Iterative refinement
workflows.how: Write a version 1, evaluate it against the requirements, write version 2 incorporating those findings. Stop when quality plateaus.

workflows.name: Domain model first
workflows.how: Define the core concepts and their relationships before writing any logic or prose. Let the model drive the structure.

workflows.name: Prototype and validate
workflows.how: Build the minimal prototype that can be shown or tested. Validate it. Then extend based only on what the validation revealed.

workflows.name: Feature slicing
workflows.how: Cut the work into thin vertical slices, each delivering end-to-end value. Complete one slice fully before starting the next.

workflows.name: Constraint propagation
workflows.how: Propagate every constraint through the solution space to eliminate impossible options early. Solve in the remaining space.

strategies.name: Simplest first
strategies.how: Choose the simplest solution that meets every requirement. Add complexity only when simplicity provably fails.

strategies.name: Defensive
strategies.how: Prefer explicit error handling, safe defaults, and conservative assumptions. Never rely on the caller to do the right thing.

strategies.name: Explicit over implicit
strategies.how: Name everything. Make every assumption visible. Prefer verbose-but-clear over terse-but-ambiguous.

strategies.name: Fail fast
strategies.how: Validate inputs at the boundary. Raise an error immediately when a precondition is violated rather than propagating bad state.

strategies.name: Optimise for change
strategies.how: Design so that the most likely future changes are cheap. Prefer interfaces that hide implementation details.

strategies.name: Data driven
strategies.how: Derive every decision from data, metrics, or evidence already in the problem. State the data source for every claim.

strategies.name: Minimise surface
strategies.how: Expose the smallest public surface that satisfies the requirements. Hide everything else.

strategies.name: Composition over inheritance
strategies.how: Prefer small composable pieces over deep hierarchies. Assemble behaviour at the call site.

strategies.name: Make it reversible
strategies.how: Prefer actions that can be undone. When an irreversible step is unavoidable, make it explicit and gated.

strategies.name: Locality
strategies.how: Keep things that change together close together. Minimise the distance between a decision and its effects.

strategies.name: Progressive disclosure
strategies.how: Present the simple case first and the full detail only when the user needs it. Never front-load complexity.

strategies.name: Pessimistic by default
strategies.how: When uncertain between a safe and a risky option, choose the safe one. Optimise later only with evidence.
